items.span_text: the Seller hereby grants (and will cause each other Seller Party to grant, following each applicable Closing Date, to the Purchaser Licensees) a perpetual (unless terminated in accordance with Section 4.2(ii)(c)), fully paid-up, royalty-free, worldwide, non-transferable (except as set forth herein), non-exclusive license to use any and all Licensed Trademarks in the Business
items.annotator_notes: 3.2.1's own motivating sentence, and the segment yields ONE item rather than two precisely because of it. The sentence has 4.3.2's flow-down shape -- a self-performance half and a duty to bind a third party to the same act -- but the self-performance half, 'the Seller HEREBY GRANTS', is a present-tense self-executing performative: it takes full legal effect at execution, so by the time anything could be monitored the act is already done. 3.2.1 excludes that half as not obligation-bearing under IR v1's four modalities, on the identical principle as 3.2's 'will'-as-future-fact carve-out one tense earlier -- there is no future state to monitor, only the tense differs. So 4.3.2's split reduces to its item 2 alone. THE ANNOTATED HALF is genuinely future-looking: 'will cause each other Seller Party to grant, following each applicable Closing Date, to the Purchaser Licensees'. Modality MUST from 'will' as an undertaking (3.2). obligor stays 'the Seller' -- 4.3.2's item-2 rule is explicit that the obligor remains the party bearing the flow-down duty and never the third party, since the other Seller Parties are not bound by this obligation at all, only referenced as the target of the Seller's oversight duty. obligee = 'the Purchaser Licensees', named in-span as the party the grant runs to (3.5's positional test). ACTION: 'cause X to grant Y' has no exact taxonomy match, which 4.3.2 acknowledges in terms and routes to 3.4's accept-set discipline rather than to a hard-coded verb; PROCURE is my single best value on the strength of 8.8's 'arrange -> PROCURE' mapping, with GRANT carried as the alternate a reader anchoring on the underlying act would defend. object_class follows 4.3.2's v0.37 recommended third_party_ prefix convention; there is no self_ sibling here because that half is excluded. SPAN: starts at 'the Seller', not at 'Effective as of the Initial Closing Date'. That leading clause fixes the timing of the HEREBY GRANT (the excluded half), whereas this duty's own timing is 'following each applicable Closing Date' inside the parenthetical, so 3.1's minimal-complete-span rule does not pull it in. It ends at '...in the Business' -- the obligation is complete there; the trailing '(including with respect to the Purchaser Licensed Activities), including with respect to all Derivative Works ... in a manner that is the same or substantially similar ...' is further object scope. The span necessarily still CONTAINS the excluded hereby-grant, because the object of 'cause ... to grant' ('a perpetual ... license') sits after the parenthetical closes and contiguity (3.1) cannot be broken. TEMPORAL: 'following each applicable Closing Date' is 8.9's gap exactly -- _RELATIVE_RE is ^(before|after) and 'following' is one of the measured rejected prepositions (11 segments, 0.7%). Annotated per 8.9's rule as RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER(after, 'each applicable Closing Date') with known_gaps gaining relative_trigger_preposition; expected v1 outcome is UNMAPPABLE_TEMPORAL, a LOUD failure visible in criterion 1b. 3.9 trigger 3 fires (resolve_trigger() returns None throughout v1), so underspecified is true and temporal is named in missing_fields. CONDITIONS EMPTY, and the two parenthetical qualifiers were each tested against 3.8.1 rather than pattern-matched on their marker words. '(unless terminated in accordance with Section 4.2(ii)(c))' carries branch 3's marker word but fails branch 3's TEST -- 3.8.1 says in terms that marker words do not decide the destination -- because it narrows the LICENSE'S duration, not the Seller's duty to cause the grant; deleting it leaves the duty applying in identical circumstances, so 3.8.2's removal test files it as object scope. '(except as set forth herein)' qualifies non-transferability the same way. The competing reading routes the 'unless' to branch 3 with an exception_unsupported tag; I record it and reject it on the branch-3 test. underspecified would be true regardless of how 'the Purchaser Licensees' resolves; I have not asserted it in missing_fields because I cannot see the scoring registry (21 R1-R3) from this pass, and 14.2 forbids using the field to record my own uncertainty.
